title: Deterministic reconciliation for quota-override rollback across billing exports
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customers have reported invoice mismatches after operators or automated compensations trigger quota_override rollbacks mid-billing-cycle. When a quota override is created and later rolled back (either via billing-ops or automated refund/compensation tasks), the export reconciler currently emits merged invoice lines that do not deterministically reflect the rollback sequence, leading to negative line items or duplicated proration adjustments in Stripe/NetSuite exports. This ticket implements a deterministic, event-sourced approach to handle quota-override rollbacks and to surface non-idempotent export candidates before they reach accounting systems.
technical_notes: Design proposal: (1) Introduce explicit "rollback tombstone" events for quota_override changes that are stored in the usage ledger with monotonic sequence numbers; (2) Extend the export preflight to run a simulated reconciliation using the ledger window (start,end,seq_min,seq_max) producing a deterministic candidate export with a signed checksum; (3) If preflight checksum differs from last-successful-export checksum, quarantine the candidate and emit a human-review task unless the change is a pure idempotent delta; (4) Update export line generation to collapse rollback tombstones into explicit adjustment lines (not negative merges) and add metadata tags for traceability (override_id, rollback_id, seq_range); (5) Add a repair-runner that can re-emit corrected exports and mark prior exported lines as superseded to maintain auditability.

acceptance_criteria: Preflight export simulation produces a deterministic candidate with checksum for all billing windows involving quota overrides.
When a rollback occurs, the exported lines include explicit adjustment rows referencing override_id and rollback_id (no negative merged lines).
Quarantined export candidates are surfaced in the Console with a one-click operator review and a documented runbook.
Repair-runner can re-emit a corrected export and mark prior exports as superseded; end-to-end integration test against sandbox Stripe/NetSuite passes.
No statistically significant increase in export latency for normal (non-rollback) tenants (<3% p95 increase).
Unit and integration tests cover sequenced tombstones, checksum drift, and repair-runner idempotency.
